**Quick take:** Dubai Creek is the historic waterway that gave Dubai its trading roots.

- • A natural salt‑water inlet of the Persian Gulf that stretches about 9 miles (14 km) inland (From Excerpt 1)  
- • Width varies between 200 – 1,200 m and depth averages 6.5 – 7 m (From Excerpt 1)  
- • Acts as a natural port, long used for trade and transport (From Excerpt 1)  
- • Handles over 13,000 ships each year, making it a key artery for the city’s maritime commerce (From Excerpt 2)  
- • Runs southeast through the mainland, passing Port Saeed and Dubai Creek Park, ending at Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary (From Excerpt 3)  
- • Connects east‑ and west‑side neighborhoods via abras (traditional wooden boats) and four bridges (Al Maktoum, Al Garhoud, etc.) (From Excerpt 3)
